question: The roots of the polynomial \(10x^3-39x^2+29x-6\) are the height, length, and width of a rectangular box (right rectangular prism). A new rectangular box is formed by lengthening each edge of the original box by \(2\) units. What is the volume of the new box?
solution:
Evaluating the polynomial at \(-2\) makes its root factors match the new dimensions, apart from signs.

Let the original dimensions be \(a,b,c\), and write
\[
f(x)=10x^3-39x^2+29x-6.
\]
Because \(a,b,c\) are its roots and its leading coefficient is \(10\),
\[
f(x)=10(x-a)(x-b)(x-c).
\]
The new volume is \(V=(a+2)(b+2)(c+2)\). Substituting \(x=-2\) gives
\[
f(-2)=10(-2-a)(-2-b)(-2-c)=-10V,
\]
since each of the three factors contributes a minus sign. Meanwhile,
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(-2)
&=10(-2)^3-39(-2)^2+29(-2)-6\\
&=-80-156-58-6\\
&=-300.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
V=-\frac{f(-2)}{10}=\boxed{30}
\]
cubic units. The answer is \(\text{D}\).
